policy: Component-boundary traceability for the shell, sidebar, Header, Settings and right workbench (PARITY_TODO.md §0.1). A group records which Rust files own the behaviour of its Web sources. `ported` requires verifiable evidence (an existing Rust test function or a file under artifacts/); `partial` must name what remains; `excluded` must give a reason. Unlisted sources are reported as pending. The Agent conversation layer is tracked separately in tools/agent-migration-map.json. Historical artifact references are retained separately and never count as reproducible acceptance evidence. Named tests establish traceability only; current execution receipts are required for verification.

excluded_patterns.reason: Browser visual-smoke harness; native verification uses capture modes and Rust tests.
Browser visual-smoke harness; native verification uses capture modes and Rust tests.
Styles or fixtures used only by browser visual-smoke harnesses.
Module barrel; re-exports only. Rust modules use mod.rs/pub use.

groups.name: Style tokens and theme packs
groups.remaining: The five built-in packs and the tokens.css semantic layer are projected into Theme; installed Sub Themes from the Themes Folder project their Application target over the Neutral fallback the same way (see Installed Sub Themes). Forced-colours mode does not occur on macOS (Chromium only enters it under Windows high contrast). STANDARD_CONTROL_SIZE (the numeric mirror of --po-control-size for virtual layout) is theme::control() for controls and transcript_rows::STANDARD_CONTROL_SIZE for the Agent timeline's row geometry.

groups.name: Installed Sub Themes
groups.remaining: The Themes Folder (<data dir>/themes, guide installed once), single-file, theme.css-directory and theme.json packages, every contract and compiler check (oracle: the product's theme service over fixtures/themes/folder, all accepted themes and diagnostics identical), the starter custom-theme, catalog refresh on start-up/window activation/after Add, per-mode selection with Neutral fallback, and the menu bar Theme menu are ported. The Application target paints the shell, and the Markdown and CSV targets (built-in themes included) reach the native Markdown and CSV views (MD-7: the product cascade with the viewer host rules of document-defaults.json; only tokens that differ from Neutral are evaluated natively, and lengths such as calc() keep the Neutral value). Typography sizes are shadowed by the user's text-size preset in the product too. @media/@supports rules are validated but not evaluated.

groups.name: Typography scale and roles
groups.remaining: TYPOGRAPHY_SCALE_METRICS and the UI role sizes follow the three scales. The font catalog (five built-in entries, role resolution with product fallbacks, id normalisation), the locales.css script stacks and their GPUI projection (the first installed family plus a cascade of the installed rest, as Chromium walks font-family) are native: the interface is Geist, code Geist Mono, the terminal the Terminal Mono stack (SF Mono where installed, else Menlo), each over the content language's CJK faces. Not ported: reading the stored puppyone.desktop.typography value with its legacy migrations (part of the Electron preference import, PL-3) and Sub Theme content fonts (S-14). TypographyCatalogContext's merge of additional catalog entries has no caller in the product (main.tsx mounts the provider without entries), so the catalog is the built-in one in both apps.

groups.name: Appearance preferences and runtime
groups.remaining: Theme mode (including following the OS), theme pack, text scale, file icon theme and pointer cursors apply natively. Palette overrides and interface styles are stored but not applied. A first launch imports the Electron product's preferences (PL-3): recent Projects with the last active first, the locale, the appearance v6 document or its legacy keys (colour mode, Sub Theme, typography, pointer cursors, file icons, loading style), pane widths, experiments, files visibility, local agents, Git layout, titlebar actions and first-run sign-in; editor tab layouts and credentials are not imported (the apps keep separate data and Keychain).

groups.name: Interface styles (skins)
groups.reason: Out of scope for this round (PARITY_TODO.md §5): the native shell renders the default interface only and the Appearance page shows the interface-style row disabled. DesktopShellLocationBar (the address bar) appears only in the windows-xp composition (composition.locationBar workspace-path-v1). The Luna Blue Sub Theme (compatible-root-themes: windows-xp) belongs to the same interface; tools/import-themes.mjs skips packs not compatible with the default root theme, and assets/themes/builtin/windows-xp-luna-blue.css is not loaded by any Rust module.

groups.name: Localization runtime
groups.remaining: Catalogs are bundled rather than lazily loaded. The ICU subset covers what the catalogs use ({arg}, number, plural with =N and #); select and date/relative-time formats are not implemented. The core (bidiIsolate, the locale manifest and system-language resolution, catalog merging, the message formatter with its English fallback, Intl number/percent/currency, relative-time, list and day formatting) is localization.rs, with platform::locale_format for regional dates and text.rs for the root collation; LocalizationProvider's document lang/dir attributes have no counterpart and message-format diagnostics are not reported.

groups.name: Settings composition and controls
groups.remaining: Dialog, sidebar and rows follow settings.css geometry; checked by capture screenshots only. There is no automated pixel comparison against the Web Settings pages.

groups.name: Preferences store
groups.remaining: One persisted owner with serde defaults and legacy migration. Fields whose Web consumer has no native counterpart (share slice, editor presentation details) are not represented.

groups.name: General settings page
groups.remaining: Language and version rows are native, and the update row and the automatic-download preference run over the native update service (DS-5, see Automatic updates). There is no separate blocked state (the quit confirmation stands in) and no Squirrel fallback.

groups.name: Appearance settings page
groups.remaining: Theme mode cards, theme pack (built-in and installed, the effective mode's selection, a missing requested theme listed), Open Themes Folder and Add Theme, the content-font override notice, catalog errors and loading issues, file icons, Header elements, pointer cursors and the Default interface style row are live. Windows XP skin and the loading-style picker are retired in the native port.

groups.name: Typography settings page
groups.remaining: Scale segment and three-pane preview are ported; the preview renders with bundled fonts rather than the catalog font stacks.

groups.name: Create New settings page and entry registry
groups.remaining: Menu and settings share one registry. Folder, Markdown, text, JSON, CSV and HTML are created natively; specialised formats (documents, slides, apps) are listed but unavailable.

groups.name: Experimental settings page
groups.remaining: Same groups and rows as the Web; rows without a native consumer are shown disabled.

groups.name: Project, Git and Git Ignore settings pages
groups.remaining: Project info, repository facts (branch, upstream, sync, remotes) and Git Ignore (hidden files + exclude patterns applied to the tree) are native. The Host Server page's backup/source-service config (PuppyoneWorkspaceConfigSettings over .puppyone/config.json, see Project configuration file) and its Puppyone Cloud connection subsection (ST-2) are native. Auto-commit is not ported (experimental, out of scope).

groups.name: Other App Imports settings page
groups.remaining: The experimental sources are listed by their own names from the shared registry; Import closes Settings for the import dialog (v0.4.4 onOpenImport).

groups.name: Import dialog (sources, repositories, app folders)
groups.remaining: Sources as two-column tiles (ready first, what is still coming after), GitHub/GitLab repository clones, and the folders Obsidian, VS Code, Cursor and Typora record, added to the Homepage in place. Remote sources (Notion, Google Drive, Airtable) are not operational in the product either. An imported repository that fails to open shows the window's project-open failure rather than the dialog's Open again. Typora's recent folders are read as one key (the product's whole-file conversion fails on the dates it also keeps).

groups.name: Privacy settings page
groups.remaining: The Product Analytics switch runs over the native telemetry service (features::telemetry over platform::telemetry) with its loading, saving and failure copy; only packaged Stable builds send, after the one-time disclosure. Not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Account and plan settings pages
groups.remaining: Plan follows the 2026-11-19 redesign rather than v0.4.4: one card with the plan, its price and renewal and two 40-cell meters (agent hours with running agents half-lit, storage), the add-ons as a list, and the other plans as rows that each say what they add, a change confirmed in its own row. The Account plan row is unchanged. Native over scripted billing; not pixel-compared with v0.4.4 by design (AC-2).

groups.name: Window navigation (places and account)
groups.remaining: Home, the places (this computer, every space, Create space) and the account rows open from the place button and the Homepage brand; Sign in sits at the Header's end while signed out. Not pixel-compared at v0.4.4 5e87974ef.

groups.name: Space settings and Create space
groups.remaining: Members (rename, roles, remove, invite with its link, transfer) and Create space are native over scripted organization APIs. A failure says one fixed sentence rather than the server's words; acceptance on hosted qubits is pending (AC).

groups.name: Local Agents settings and inventory
groups.remaining: Detected agents with persisted show/hide, rescan, empty/error states and history discovery are native; the Launcher honours hidden agents. Hooks: the enrollment snapshot, one change at a time, the loading/empty/error-with-Retry rows and the file-activity preference sync are native over src/platform/agent_activity. Setup (LocalAgentSetupSection): the suggestion preference and Restore, operation rows (step n/3 · status, View, Stop), the request-failed alert with Refresh, the Set up Agents directory, and the launcher presentation (suggested and running activations between the detected and the bundled Agents) over the setup registry, the companion-app scan and the advisor (local-agents 98.8%, agent-hooks 98.9%). Not ported: returning focus to the launcher after a dialog closes; native discovery has no failed scans, so entries are never `unknown`.

groups.name: Local Agent activation
groups.remaining: The store (snapshots by epoch and revision), the dialog (consent or guided text, the three steps, the background note, Installation details with publisher and version, the Claude Chat note, step circles with checks, status, error and retained notes, the request-failed alert, Cancel/Install, Stop/Try again/Guide/Check/Continue in background/Close) and the service behind it (plans per window, three at once, journal v2, interrupted on restart, the reviewed codex/cursor recipes with digest, archive and lease checks shared with the Electron product's ~/.puppyone/agent-runtimes) are native. agent-activation 96.7% / 94.0%: the light backdrop blur (D-3) and 20.8px line heights rounded to device pixels. Not ported: the v1 journal migration (the native journal starts at v2), and pixel comparison of the progress states.

groups.name: Local Agent installation discovery store
groups.remaining: Discovery runs in-process on a worker; Settings and the launchers own their scans (generations drop stale results) and rescan when an activation installs a CLI. Not ported: one shared store per window and progress events.

groups.name: Local Agent installation IPC (Electron bridge)
groups.reason: The preload IPC client and the validation of its snapshots; native discovery is a function call (local_agent_inventory::discover) with typed results.

groups.name: Agent file-activity permission styles (unused)
groups.reason: No component renders the .desktop-agent-activity-permission-* classes (grep over src, packages and electron at 6dee919d); the stylesheet is not imported.

groups.name: Model Connections settings
groups.remaining: List, add/edit and detail flow with Keychain credentials. Local service discovery, tool-support verification and managed (cloud) connections are not ported.

groups.name: Header and window chrome
groups.remaining: Project button, place menu (address, brand-blue Cloud mark, who can open it), Agents marks, Changes status icons and Header coachmarks are native. Share and the Cloud Header tint were retired in qubits@6f896add1 and qubits@343998d0c. The update button (DesktopUpdateTitlebarButton) is native, see Automatic updates.

groups.name: Project menu, location switcher and project rail
groups.remaining: v0.4.4: the title bar reads [place] / [folder]; the folder menu lists the current place's folders (projectMenuGroups) and Home only where no place menu is; the rail hides the folder segment only. Not pixel-compared at v0.4.4 5e87974ef. ProjectRowActions (a folder: Copy path, Rename, who can open it, Unlink; a Cloud entry: Rename and Delete, as permitted) is native in project_actions.rs for the Homepage, the rail and the menu. The menu's project mark reuses the Homepage list icon (brand-blue Cloud, linked badge) instead of ProjectContextAssetMark's accent mix with a 10% fill. Not ported: arrow, Home and End walking of menu items (desktopMenuKeyboard) and dragging a rail project out as a Finder folder (projectRootDrag). Custom project icons (useProjectAppearanceCatalog: an emoji or image per project from the project-appearance store) are not read; v0.4.4 has no control that sets one (projectAppearance.chooseIcon/setEmoji have no renderer caller), so the rail draws each project's default mark.

groups.name: Home page
groups.remaining: The Grid folder wall and List with their remembered switch, sort, row actions, the New project split button, template links (pasted on the page or opened) and dragging a project out as its path are native. The create dialog asks who can open the project first (qubits@686d41c49); All my devices waits for the other computers (DV). The place filter and Paste template link were retired. The homepage has not been pixel-compared at qubits@686d41c49. TemplateImportCard (with useProjectTemplateImport), LinkedCloudProjectButton (opens the folder's own Cloud project), OnboardingEntryMenu (New project, the arrow holding Open a folder and Import with its marks) and the single OnboardingPrimarySection slot are native.

groups.name: Homepage place groups
groups.remaining: v0.4.4: This computer, then every space (even empty, with its mark, plan, Owner and Members & plan), then shared projects without a known space, then other computers (gated off). A place asked for from the title bar is scrolled to and lit (useProjectGroupFocus). Grid of 5×120px cells with 10px gutters; checked by offscreen capture, not pixel-compared at v0.4.4 5e87974ef. The toolbar menus (OnboardingToolbarMenu, useOnboardingMenu) open centred under their control on PopoverMenu with outside-press and Escape dismissal and focus restore; arrow, Home and End walking of their items is not ported.

groups.name: Project folder availability and relocation
groups.remaining: Statuses (available, missing, disk not connected, not permitted, not a folder), the folder found renamed in place by its dev:ino identity, the Homepage caption and dialog, the window notice, and relocation (the record moves; a window showing it reopens it there) are native. Find it… opens the system picker where it last was (GPUI's open panel takes no starting folder). Main's one-time candidate tokens are not needed in one process; the chosen folder is probed again before use. A relocated folder that had been shared is not offered again (other computers are off in this release). A folder read failure in the workbench does not yet re-check its availability; activation does.

groups.name: Who can open it (project audience)
groups.remaining: v0.4.4 shows the audience only in the Homepage project menu (projectAudience in MinimalOnboarding): devices, and a team copy to open or make; the place menu no longer carries it, and the Cloud copy's problem and Send rows have no producer. Turning All my devices on or off is gated off with hosts. No pixel comparison.

groups.name: Cloud spaces and team publication
groups.remaining: Discovery, the per-account cache, the publication intent and the explicit organization target are native over scripted transports; acceptance against a real Cloud is pending (VA-1).

groups.name: Pane frames, edges and the Explorer column
groups.remaining: One PaneLayout entity owns both panes (open state, widths, edge drag, keyboard resize, the 360ms frame motion and the window minimum); PaneStack paints each pane's content plane at its open width under the editor, which covers instead of clipping it, so the cached panes are reused through the motion. The frame motion runs on a FrameTimeline (a late frame advances it by at most 33ms). The focused edge shows its hover stroke instead of the product's 2px focus outline, and the collapsed right edge takes no keys. usePaneResizeDrag's pointer session (commit on release, roll back on cancel or when the controlled pane changes) is PaneLayout's edge drag; its other consumer, the Changes sidebar's section resizer (useGitSidebarPanelLayout), is drawn as a static divider and cannot be dragged. The resolved pane layout reaches the Explorer frame through the PaneLayout entity rather than a React context (DesktopPaneLayoutContext); right-to-left mirroring of the edges' pointer and arrow resizing (auxiliarySidebarGeometry) is not applied.

groups.name: Explorer tree and file actions
groups.remaining: Local resource mutations now drain and rebind retained Working Copies; Explorer sessions retain trees, selection, scroll and clipboard across projects and revalidate loaded folders. Extension-changing viewer transitions (E-2), resource-scoped mutation queues (E-3), the root directory subscription and reference drags into the Agent composer and the terminal are native. Pinned files (ExplorerPinnedFiles, explorerPins) are app/explorer/pins.rs, kept per project in Preferences; the per-project Explorer session (useProjectExplorerSession) is app/explorer/session.rs, without the product's cap of 12 retained sessions. Paste and duplicate (fileTransfer) run entry by entry and report through the clipboard notice, but a cut leaves the clipboard when its paste starts, so failed cut entries are not kept. Entries drag out to other apps as files (resourceDragExport / useResourceDragExport; EX-4): an AppKit dragging session with one file URL per entry and the paths as text; Chromium's single-file DownloadURL projection is not mirrored. The list-end New row (list_end_row) rides after the last row inside the uniform_list and moves with the disclosure motion, but it does not pin to the scrollport bottom once the tree overflows: useStickyListEnd's sticky band (DesktopDataWorkspaceSurface passes explorerListEndPlacement="sticky"), its hidden-content fade and the scroll-padding it publishes are not ported. Multi-root composition is not ported; strict visual and OS drag parity are unverified.

groups.name: Sidebar footer navigation and help
groups.remaining: Settings and Help (product FeedbackHelpIcon) are native in the footer with the product geometry, utility colour, no divider and the tree edge fade; like the product, Git is not in the footer (Changes lives in the Header). Plugins (excluded with Viewer plugins) and the Project Rail utilities are not ported, and the rail/top navigation variants are unreachable (see Unused App Shell leftovers); the busy pulse grid is a native stand-in for FloatingNoticeStack.

groups.name: Workbench launcher
groups.remaining: Detected agents, the Built-in Agent + Terminal group, rescan, History and discovery status are native and respect hidden agents; Codex uses the monochrome ChatGPT mark like AgentMonochromeBrandImage. Install guides and per-agent activation are not ported. The recipe catalog (agentChatCreationRecipes: English-label order with the bundled Built-in Agent last; a hidden local Agent hides its chat runtime, never the built-in) is native in local_agents::chat_recipes and the inventory.

groups.name: Workbench tabs, split layout and close flow
groups.remaining: 38px tab bar with compact/overflow modes, brand icons with the running-chat dot (AuxiliaryWorkbenchStatus), tab context menu, drag split and close confirmation are native. Session-header motion (200ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1) from the drawn position; new tabs grow from their neighbour, overflow from the create control; off while dragging, inserting or with reduced motion), the tab-move preview 18px before and 12px below the pointer, and the creation failure (a History conversation that cannot resume returns its tab to the launcher with a Retry/Dismiss notice) are native. Not ported: the preview's popover shadow (GPUI draws it under the transparent body). The viewport, item views retained across moves between groups (usePersistentWorkbenchItemHosts / AuxiliaryWorkbenchItemHostSlot: one view per item instead of reparented DOM hosts), the split resize gesture clamped to both sides' minimum sizes, roving tab focus (arrows, Home, End) and the session-header layout are native in the same files. The per-project workbench is Workbench.projects keyed by root, not the main process's project-session stream (generation, closing failures, 5s poll), which one process does not need; derived-click suppression, the header item type and DOM tab/panel ids are React plumbing with no counterpart. Right-to-left arrow mirroring is not applied.

groups.name: Workbench header motion, tab-move preview and creation failure
groups.remaining: Native resume errors are free text, so the notice uses the generic itemLoadFailed message instead of the per-code openError messages; the pixel lab captures the header at rest (as the reference finishes animations).

groups.name: Workbench render failure boundaries
groups.reason: React error boundaries catch exceptions thrown while rendering. Native render functions return elements and cannot throw; a failing item host (Agent runtime, PTY) is already isolated per tab and reported in that tab's own content (failed session card, terminal system line), and process-level supervision is A-14/A-16.

groups.name: Changes panel (source control)
groups.remaining: Collapsible Staged/Unstaged/Merge/Committed panels with Commit and Stage and Commit (product default message), Pull notice and Push are native and localized. A selected change opens WorkingFileDetail in place (Open file / Stage / Unstage / Discard) over the Diff Registry: the unified text diff (numbered lines, hunk separators, wrapping) and the binary summary (format, before/after sizes, open current file), framed by GitFileDiffSurface. History is the day-grouped timeline with change totals and a four-file preview; a commit opens its summary (HEAD, copyable id, totals) and file diffs. As in the Web (git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree), a folder anywhere inside a work tree is managed and lists the whole repository with repository-relative paths; staging, discarding, diffs and Open file act only on changes inside the opened folder (the Web passes repository paths as folder-relative pathspecs, which fails from a subfolder). Discard and Abort ask first through the system confirmation (the product's window.confirm); Pull, Push and Publish run without one, as in the product, and a failed operation is the product's Git error dialog (GT-3). A branch that tracks nothing is published to the sync target (GT-1); a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert in progress offers Continue and Abort (GT-2). A Word document diffs as the product's body-text redline (docx-redline: word/document.xml read within DOCX_REDLINE_BUDGET, blocks aligned on unique anchors and a weighted edit distance, word-level segments; document state, totals, changed blocks, the limit and the fidelity note), built on the Git worker together with the patch instead of in a Web Worker, so it is not cached (WeightedTtlLruCache, clearFormatAwareDiffCaches), has no 20 s worker timeout and no loading state of its own. A folder outside a repository offers Enable version control (git init, GitRepositorySetupAction) without the product's pending label; the Cloud backup card (GitRemotePrompt) is native. Sections size by their rows (at most nine, never below 72px) but the drag and keyboard resize between sections is not ported, and focus does not move to the view header when the list and a detail swap (useGitViewNavigationFocus). The shared DesktopEntryState layout is not used: a folder that is not a repository shows a centred note with Enable. The incoming-change review belongs to Project Reach (excluded).

groups.name: Terminal surface
groups.remaining: Terminal colours come from the pack. The font is the product's Terminal Mono stack; cells follow xterm's WebGL renderer (the W advance floored to device pixels; Blink's whole-pixel font box, x1.24, floored; glyphs on the cell grid on device pixels), with the session padding (14/0/16/16), FitAddon's fit, 6000 lines of scrollback, weight 450/700, the blinking block cursor, the unfocused outline and xterm's cursor initialisation, box drawing/blocks/shades/Powerline from the product's xterm definitions (tools/import-xterm-glyphs.mjs), the hovered link's underline and click activation, the default-style scrollbar (12px lane, 8px thumb while hovered or 900 ms after a scroll), grey system lines for exits and launch failures and the top notice stack. Pixel suite `terminal`: 95.3% with identical geometry; xterm's canvas rasterises glyphs with macOS font smoothing, GPUI without. Not ported: the classic-interface scrollbar (P3 interface styles), xterm checkpoint restore and Unicode 11 width tables (vt100 uses unicode-width).

groups.name: Shared overlays, dialogs and tooltips
groups.remaining: Dialogs and tooltips use GPUI Kit with product tokens. The product scrollbar (scrollbars.css with ScrollbarActivity) is Kit's base scrollbar over each scroll owner: a 12px lane, the thumb transparent at rest and 8px / 2px inset while the owner is hovered (vendor patch) or for 900 ms after it scrolls, the hover colour over the thumb; Settings, Homepage, Explorer, Source Control, History, Agent transcript/history/picker/dock, launcher, menus, dialogs and the PDF/database viewers carry it. The classic-interface arrow buttons belong to the P3 interface styles; the light backdrop composites darker than Chromium (Settings light 86%, under investigation). Tooltip.tsx's explicit per-control wrap is the native `.tooltip(text)` (ui::components::tooltip over Kit's Tooltip); its placement hint, shortcut line, overflow-only labels, hover-only trigger and disableTooltipHints are not carried by the native helper. DesktopOverlayPortal's copy of the appearance, typography and theme presets onto the portal root has no native counterpart: dialogs and menus read the window's active appearance. A modal's inert surroundings (inertHold) are the dialog layer's backdrop, which takes every press and key; holdHoverUntilPointerUse (pointerRest: what a closing dialog uncovers does not light up until the pointer is used) is not ported.

groups.name: Markdown viewer (native editor)
groups.remaining: Native live preview and source mode: headings, emphasis, links and wiki links, lists, tasks, quotes, rules, highlighted code blocks, editable tables, front matter, callouts (with folding), footnotes, math (as Unicode text, not KaTeX), images in image lines, inline HTML of the inline-editable profile, HTML blocks with Markdown inside, and the block-drag experiment (PARITY_TODO §7). Not native: Mermaid, MDX, images beside text, media in inline HTML runs, AI edit review, document navigation, heading outline, table column resize. The window-level format keys (markdownFormatShortcutBridge: Cmd+B/I/U/D and Cmd+Shift+X, which Chromium would otherwise take) are GPUI key bindings in the editor's key context, so no main-process bridge is needed.

groups.name: Text, JSON and code viewers and shared editor infrastructure
groups.remaining: Text, JSON and code files open in the native code editor: tree-sitter highlighting per the product's language resolution, indent guides, bracket matching, selection matches, trailing whitespace, folds, find, IME, multi-cursor, JSON formatting (normalizeContent) and the conflict banner. Like the product's CodeMirror viewer there is no JSON validation or language service; CodeMirror's exact token palette and metrics are not pixel-compared.

groups.name: CSV table viewer
groups.remaining: Native table, source mode, structure operations, column widths, references and find (PARITY_TODO N9). Workspace reference resolution through the product link graph is not ported.

groups.name: HTML viewer (Interact, Edit, Source)
groups.remaining: Interact runs the page in the system WebView; Edit runs the product's HtmlVisualSurface (source index, edit compiler, projection, frame bridge, toolbar, block rail, text input) bundled from the product into the WebView, with the native code editor owning text, history and saves; Source is the native code editor. Not pixel-compared; the Edit page's toolbar uses the bundled Geist Sans and the active Sub Theme tokens. Cloud documents cannot import images (no provider write); the standalone options menu (HtmlViewMenu) is the pane menu instead. v0.4.4 folder access and links are native: a page naming the folder picker is asked about before it runs (the product's HtmlFolderAccessDialog on the window's dialog layer through editor::question, VW-4: 420px, Don't allow holds the focus, closing declines), the allowance is kept per page path and text digest (at most 200), and an allowed page runs offline, locked to itself, with the folder bridge over the workspace provider and a host-kept localStorage (256 K characters). The page is the web view's own document, so it posts through window.ipc. Clicked links resolve through document navigation (workspace documents open in the workbench, addresses in the browser) with the four failure notices. The host's scripts lead the page's head, ahead of its own policy, so the author's CSP is never loosened with a nonce. Listed files carry no modification time. The consent queue (htmlFolderAccessConsent) is editor::question shown as the app's dialog (app/dialogs/question.rs); a second question replaces the open one instead of waiting its turn, and a page closed while it waits does not withdraw its question.

groups.name: Viewer registry
groups.remaining: Markdown and CSV / TSV open in their native editors, other text files in the native code editor; HTML, PDF, image, audio/video, Office and database documents open in their viewers. Context-map, app and PuppyFlow viewers have no native implementation.

groups.name: Editor pane chrome and actions menu
groups.remaining: Native ⋯ handle, actions menu (live / source, CSV view items, find, open externally, close) and find bar for the single pane; multi-pane runtime is tracked under the editor workbench group. Open in default app (useExternalFileOpen) is Command::OpenExternal and the Explorer's Open in Default App over platform::desktop::open (/usr/bin/open, files only); a failure shows as the window's error.

groups.name: Editor document session
groups.remaining: The retained working-copy registry, shared storage identity, late snapshots, external observation and close/resource-operation drains are implemented in src/editor/workbench and src/documents. Idle auto-save and window-blur flushing follow the reviewed qubits contract. Real OS input, WebView interaction and cross-platform acceptance still require native application execution; model and synthetic tests do not establish those results.

groups.name: Editor workbench: splits, tabs, pane move and file drop
groups.remaining: Local tabs/MRU, recursive panes, retained documents/projects and layout persistence run in the real Shell. Same-workspace single-file Explorer drops focus existing views, fill empty panes or split at an edge, with a preview and target-lifetime fencing. Cloud navigation/drafts, full pane view state, cross-root/native external-drop authority, complete keyboard/accessibility and strict pixel parity remain incomplete. useInteractionTermination: GPUI ends a drag or split resize on mouse-up; the product's Escape, window-blur, page-hide and HTML dragend/drop terminations of a pointer session are not ported.

groups.name: Editor and shared-ui stylesheets (product tokens in native styles)
groups.remaining: Token values are imported from the product CSS (tools/import-editor-theme.mjs → assets/editor); the rules are re-expressed per element in Rust styles. Floating notices and overflow dots have native consumers (see Floating notices and Shared buttons and overflow dots); the remaining shared-ui patterns have none yet.

groups.name: Cloud Homepage catalog and opening choices
groups.remaining: A local folder and its Cloud project are two entries; the last catalog stands in until the fresh one, cached per account. Entries carry their space (org_id) for the audience groups. No pixel comparison with Cloud rows yet.

groups.name: Cloud repository association and Header switch
groups.remaining: The product has no Local/Cloud Header switch: the place menu says who can open a folder and opens its Cloud copy; a lost link is a problem row with Disconnect (qubits@9035af9e2). The place menu and LocalFolderCloudNotice have not been pixel-compared.

groups.name: Cloud explicit opening and failures
groups.remaining: Concurrent-open coalescing, the recovery dialog's Details disclosure and pixel comparison of the loading and recovery states remain.

groups.name: Cloud live file provider
groups.remaining: Scope targets, copy/import, viewer preview resources (Office/database temp files, HTML data-URL projection) and real-backend acceptance are not covered.

groups.name: Cloud History
groups.remaining: The hosted sidebar is native; the graph and the two-pane page are the services History group. No pixel comparison.

groups.name: Cloud file workspace
groups.remaining: The hosted shell reuses the native Explorer, editor and viewers; authority changes revoke the selection, reopening rebinds retained Working Copies, and a failed subscription shows the workspace notice with Retry. Cloud preview resources (Office/database temp files, HTML data-URL projection), Scope targets and real-backend acceptance remain; the floating notices are not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Cloud first publication
groups.remaining: The coordinator (an explicit organization target with no fallback, journal v2 with v1 migration, idempotent creation, keychain secret, URL-scoped secure helper, immutable push with lease, remote-truth reconciliation, explicit cleanup) and the activation / running / resume pictures are native. The push receipt endpoint (readInitialPushReceipt) is not consulted (ls-remote only); the transfer meter, the hero artwork and pixel comparison are not ported; the initialization telemetry is not ported; acceptance against a real Cloud Git host is pending. The cross-process Cloud Git operation lease (cloud-git-operation-lease.mjs: a heartbeat lease file in the repository's common dir, held through publication and while detaching the puppyone remote) is not ported; the native app is single-instance and a window's publication model runs one publication at a time.

groups.name: Terminal legacy session hosts (unreachable)
groups.reason: Not reachable from the product entry at v0.4.0 (import walk from every non-test, non-harness module): the terminal-owned session header, overflow, tab moves, split groups and session hosts survive only for the visual-smoke harnesses. Production terminals are Auxiliary Workbench items (TerminalWorkbenchContribution), so their tabs, overflow, moves and splits are the shared workbench ones (src/features/workbench). useWorkbenchPaneContentHandleReveal is imported only by the unreachable useTerminalPaneContentHandleReveal re-export.

groups.name: Terminal workbench item
groups.note: Terminal items are titled by the project folder with the launcher as their icon; the overflow detail is 'folder — status'; a starting or running session confirms before closing; 32 terminals per project; sessions live per project and survive project switches; the PTY bridge, its control queue and process budget are platform::terminal. The terminal feature gate is the header's terminal preference. Of terminalSessions.ts production uses only the session types (its reducer serves the unreachable legacy hosts).

groups.name: Git refresh scheduling
groups.note: No status polling: reads come from debounced invalidations (250 ms) of the working tree (the root watcher) and the repository metadata (an OS watcher on the Git, common and refs directories, lock files, objects and cookies filtered, 120 ms bursts), from focus once 5 s stale, and from mutations. The upstream's remote is fetched silently (--prune) while focused: on first status (15 s gap), every 180 s and on focus once 60 s stale; a local-only branch never touches the network. Not ported: the per-workspace snapshot cache and the watcher's re-arm backoff (notify re-subscribes itself).

groups.name: Header coachmarks
groups.remaining: useHeaderCoachmarks (once per project entry for the Agent, on the first local change for Changes, Changes queued behind the Agent, acknowledged by opening either panel, persisted as puppyone.desktop.headerCoachmarks.v1 and imported, repeated by enableAlwaysShowOnboardingCoachmarks) and the overlay (320px, end-aligned 10px below its entry, the accent-lit entry, glyph tile, title, body, Later / primary; outside press dismisses) are native. Not ported: Escape dismissal (GPUI keys need focus, the overlay takes none), the toolbar-placement variant, pixel comparison against the product overlay.

groups.name: Cloud Automation route (experimental)
groups.reason: Experimental enableCloudAutomation, off by default; not ported, awaiting a decision (C-14.1). The Automation feature itself (src/features/automation: page, dialogs, templates, bindings and styles) is reachable only through AutomationRouteSection's lazy import, and nothing in v0.4.4 imports that section.

groups.name: Cloud Branches section
groups.reason: A route with no entry in the product: nothing navigates to it, so it has no native page.

groups.name: Cloud Agent client
groups.remaining: Verified over scripted and loopback services only: hosted acceptance and two windows on one session (C-10.6, ISSUE-112) need a real backend.

groups.name: Cloud organization and Billing
groups.remaining: Settings › Plan reads one space's billing through workspace::cloud::billing with the in-memory read cache (30 s, keyed by session, space and API). Quotes and checkout are verified against scripted servers; acceptance on hosted qubits is pending (AC).

groups.name: Cloud History graph model
groups.remaining: The graph model is native; the two-pane History page and its graph visual went with the services Hub (qubits@6f896add1). Local Git topology (gitTopology.ts) is not used; no pixel comparison.

groups.name: Cloud shared presentation and session hooks
groups.remaining: What the services Hub left behind and the product still uses: the activation hero and Cloud marks, the shared Cloud styles, the session and sign-in hooks, the project recovery state and the repository target. The Hub itself was retired in qubits@6f896add1 (native dialog removed in puppyone@4d817e857). No pixel comparison.

groups.name: Retired Cloud services Hub (unreachable)
groups.reason: qubits@6f896add1 retired the Cloud services Hub (Overview, Access, MCP, CLI, Team, Settings, History and Billing pages). These files are still in the tree at qubits@686d41c49 but nothing reaches them from src/main.tsx or electron/app-entry.mjs except their own barrels. The native dialog was removed in puppyone@4d817e857; workspace::cloud::billing stays for Settings › Plan.

groups.name: Cloud sign-in surfaces
groups.remaining: Browser OAuth, social sign-in, Keychain and several processes need real-environment acceptance (C-2.6).

groups.name: Cloud workspace plumbing
groups.remaining: Hosted acceptance with E2B and Fly providers (C-6.11, C-15.4).

groups.name: Cloud API client
groups.remaining: Projects, spaces (GET /organizations/, POST /auth/personal-space), Idempotency-Key creation and billing are native over scripted transports. The access-point and dashboard calls went with the services Hub. cloudApi.ts also carries Automation calls, which follow their experimental feature (C-14.1).

groups.name: Cloud session and sign-in (main process)
groups.remaining: Browser OAuth, social sign-in, Keychain and several processes need real-environment acceptance (C-2.6). cloud-runtime.mjs's composition (auth and the Cloud API on Chromium's net stack) is the auth service's one reqwest client with the system proxy resolved the way Chromium does (platform::proxy, PAC included).

groups.name: Cloud workspace streams and preview bytes (main process)
groups.remaining: Hosted acceptance with E2B and Fly providers (C-6.11, C-10.6, C-15.4).

groups.name: Cloud IPC
groups.reason: Electron's process boundary. The native app is one process (D-1), so these calls go directly to the models.

groups.name: Project place menu and local Cloud notice
groups.remaining: v0.4.4: the place button (SpaceMark, Cloud or this computer, at most 160px, with the link's state) opens navigation only; the address, audience and History rows are gone. LocalFolderCloudNotice and CloudLinkDisconnectDialog are native. Not pixel-compared at v0.4.4 5e87974ef.

groups.name: Cloud workspace Agents
groups.remaining: The Header (live marks, the resting stack, the empty seat), the hover card, the persistent request card, the Agents dialog with its two-step invite and paste drawing, Agent avatars and creatures, and the command-based at-work rule (qubits@686d41c49) are native over scripted services. Hosted acceptance against a real backend and a pixel comparison remain; the Header mark's hop moves but does not tilt.

groups.name: Window project, opening surface and file mode
groups.remaining: File mode windows, the opening surface and newer-choice replacement are native; the window's project state is held by the Shell's fields rather than one store (windowProjectStore), with the same visible behaviour. The file window's view menu (EditorViewModeMenu: 15px icons, a quiet trailing check, bounded height), the launch's restoring screen (RestoringWorkspaceScreen: the neutral area LoadingMark under a drag region) and ProjectNavigationFailure (420px, Close and Retry; a Cloud failure shows its code and request id with Copy details) are native.

groups.name: PDF viewer
groups.remaining: PDFium renders the pages natively instead of Chromium's embedded viewer (toolbar=0&navpanes=0); the pending state, budget/timeout/resource failures with Retry and the pane's Reload follow PdfViewer. The resource preflight is a local read, so HTTP MIME/length admission has no counterpart, and page content is the engine's rendering rather than a pixel contract.

groups.name: Image, audio and video viewers
groups.remaining: Images decode natively (AVIF through the platform codec) with the pending label and the unavailable state with Retry; audio and video play in the system web engine, which reports a media error so the surface shows the product's failure with Retry. Native controls are WebKit's, not Chromium's, and the audio card's icon uses the default file icon theme.

groups.name: Database viewer
groups.remaining: SQLite follows the product budget, object list, typed cells, recovery checks, idle sleep and snapshot restart, with the product toolbar, sticky grid and pager; DuckDB files (.duckdb, .ddb) route to binary-placeholder rather than embedding libduckdb. Object tabs have no arrow-key focus movement, and sidecar files are not watched as document dependencies.

groups.name: Office viewer
groups.remaining: The product's OfficeViewer (with its security preflight, validation and text-fallback workers) is bundled from the pinned sources and runs in WKWebView; .doc/.rtf conversion is the macOS textutil bridge. WebKit, not Chromium, renders the documents, and the bundle adapts TextDecoder on resizable buffers and DOMParser with a leading BOM. The editor task scheduler, host leases and worker host run inside the page rather than sharing the workbench's document barriers, and Office editor actions (unused by the product) are not offered.

groups.name: PuppyFlow editor
groups.remaining: The product's PuppyFlowViewer and StructuredDocumentModel are bundled from the pinned sources and run in WKWebView; the native surface owns the text, saves, reloads, menu undo/redo and read-only input. Run validates enabled steps only, as in the product. The theme switch rebuilds the page on the current text, which resets its history.

groups.name: Excalidraw whiteboard
groups.remaining: The fixed on-demand Excalidraw pack and native document-generation ownership are qualified by actual archive/model tests and GPUI transport acceptance. Real OS canvas drawing, IME, undo keyboard handling and embedded HTML interaction remain unqualified; actual frame latency and full interaction budgets still need native-window evidence. Third-party pack activation, signatures and uninstall are separate.

groups.name: Context Map viewer
groups.remaining: The product's ContextMapViewer (graph loading, radial/canvas/layered layouts, routing, wheel navigation, line filters) runs in WKWebView over native workspace reads, with its layout switch and filters in the native pane menu and workspace changes bumping its revision. Its retained view state (layout mode) lives for the page, not the document model owner, and document dependency tracking is the root watch rather than per-path.

groups.name: App Preview viewer and runtime
groups.remaining: The product's AppPreviewViewer runs in WKWebView over the ported runtime. A manifest command named `node` runs the person's Node rather than the app's bundled runtime, HTTPS local servers count as ready once they accept a connection, and Cloud workspaces have no App Preview runtime (as in the product's Cloud data port). App setup detection and manifest writing (appPreviewCreation: candidate scripts, package manager, framework, command line) run inside the bundled product page, which tools/app-preview-entry.tsx wires to the host's listChildren/readFile.

groups.name: Editor document host
groups.remaining: The native DocumentEditor opens the resolved contribution's surface with its input (text within MAX_TEXT_BYTES, a lease-checked resource, or none), read-only and appearance, pane menu entries and find, and hands surfaces their workspace. The React suspense, lazy viewer loading and DOM readiness signals are GPUI's own rendering; the AI edit overlay (aiEditFile) is not passed to surfaces.

groups.name: Editor resource and runtime plumbing
groups.remaining: Document inputs, resource leases and change matching are the native document sessions and PreviewResource leases; background work runs on GPUI's executors. The renderer task scheduler, host leases and worker host run inside the bundled product pages (Office), and the per-path dependency index is replaced by document and root watches. DocumentAssetImport is the HTML visual editor's native image import.

groups.name: Editor registry contracts
groups.remaining: Viewer capability, contract and manifest checks and Viewer Pack routing and manifest validation are native; the pack host API has no runtime to serve (see Viewer Packs).

groups.name: Viewer Packs
groups.remaining: The product ships with externalViewerPacks disabled (package.json puppyoneCapabilities), so no pack runtime runs: the native build keeps the same eligibility, routing, chooser and strict manifest validation, without the signed package store, isolated pack surface or resource broker.

groups.name: Editor conflict banner and save chip
groups.remaining: Conflict blocks resolve as one undoable local edit (keep current / incoming, all or one block; read-only shows the banner without actions), and the save chip with its failure overlay follows EditorSaveButton; the chip's pixel parity is not separately verified.

groups.name: Document navigation
groups.remaining: Workspace and external references (URLs, Markdown and wiki links, workspace paths) resolve through the native reference index; the Markdown-specific link graph belongs to the advanced Markdown phase.

groups.name: Other computers: access side and device folder provider
Other computers: PuppyOne Host
groups.remaining: System sleep and wake are not observed (the 30 s silence check reconnects after wake); the file service and terminals run in the host process rather than separate utility processes; only the macOS login entry (LaunchAgent) is written, not XDG autostart or a Windows login item; Git history operations (graph, commit_detail) are not offered to other computers.

groups.name: Other computers: Homepage, sharing dialog and remote tools
groups.remaining: No reference-image comparison yet for the remote folder list, the sharing dialog or the remote tools; the native confirmations are product dialogs rather than system alerts.

groups.name: Project Reach (experimental)
groups.reason: The decision point for the Project Reach experiment (experimentalSettings.enableProjectReach, default false), read by App.tsx and SourceControlSidebar.tsx to fork into Reach surfaces; Reach is out of scope, so the native app always takes the existing path. Project Reach is out of scope. These run only when useProjectReachExperience() is on: App.tsx applies reachHeaderChangesStatus under projectReachEnabled, and SourceControlSidebar swaps in getReachSyncWording / getReachSidebarModelWording and renders IncomingChangesRegion (useIncomingChangeReview with active: projectReach) instead of GitIncomingUpdateNotice; incoming-changes.css styles only IncomingChangesRegion.

groups.name: AI edit review (dormant preference)
groups.reason: AI edit review only runs when the aiEditAssistEnabled preference is true; it defaults to false and no Settings control sets it (only the legacy puppyone.desktop.aiEditAssist localStorage key), so in the product App passes activeAiEditRequest=null. The Rust port does not implement AI edit review (see Markdown viewer). useAiEditReviewRequest loads only under the same preference; the AI edit overlay is already noted as not passed to surfaces in the Editor document host group.

groups.name: Agent brand catalog and marks
groups.remaining: AGENT_BRAND_CATALOG (ids, names, aliases, retired ids, optical scale, light/dark marks) and resolveAgentBrand's whole-word matching are ui::agent_brands; AgentBrandImage is agent_brands::image (theme mark at its optical scale) and the monochrome ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, Cursor and Pi marks are drawn in the surface's text colour. Marks are embedded by src/assets.rs rather than served from public/ paths, so RENDERER_ASSET_PATHS survives only as the importer's file list; the PuppyOne brand entries of that catalog (assets/brand/puppy-*.svg) are drawn by the Homepage and first-run screens.

groups.name: Editor appearance and typography change signals
groups.remaining: The appearance revision and the typography change event are one Appearance global with a single writer (Appearance::apply), so every view re-renders with the new palette and type scale instead of subscribing to a revision or a DOM event. Native editors paint the inactive selection colour (--po-*-selection-inactive-bg) when they lose focus; the document-wide data-po-native-selection / data-po-window-active projection for plain DOM text has no counterpart because GPUI labels are not text-selectable.

groups.name: Data port contracts, resource paths and workspace content changes
groups.remaining: The DataPort / Workspace contracts are the admitted Workspace handle (ResourceId, RelativePath validation, capabilities, leases, watches); rebasing paths after a rename or move is Tree::rebind and the editor's resource operations; content changes arrive as root watch events that the Explorer session turns into ContentChanged. There is no puppyone-local:// resource URI string identity or bounded 128-entry WorkspaceContentChange log, and WorkbenchWorkspaceContext's multi-folder events are out of scope (multi-root workspaces); one Workspace is one folder.

groups.name: File format registry
groups.remaining: Name and MIME resolution, filename globs, matched and resolved extensions, semantic kinds, text-likeness and preferred MIME types run over the imported product table. FilePreviewKind (getFilePreviewKind / getPreviewKindForFormat) is not projected: the editor registry picks the surface from defaultViewer directly.

groups.name: Embedded frame scroll and pointer relay
groups.remaining: GPUI surfaces report their scroll through Surface::scroll_state and take the host's chrome inset through set_chrome_inset (text, Markdown, code and CSV), and the file window reads the pointer directly for its chrome reveal. WebView-hosted documents (HTML and other bundled product pages) keep the trait defaults: their scroll and pointer are not relayed to the host and they do not read --po-editor-chrome-inset-block-start.

groups.name: Explorer reference drag payload
groups.remaining: Explorer entries drag as one in-process ResourceDrag (workspace-relative paths, the source workspace and a label) that editor panes, terminals and the Agent panel admit, and that leaves the window as files. The versioned JSON DataTransfer payload, its parsing limits and classifyReferenceDataTransfer's file / text-URI classification are DOM transport with no native counterpart; entries of a workspace without a local root (Cloud) give terminals and the Agent no paths.

groups.name: File icon themes and glyphs
groups.remaining: Every theme's FileGlyphIcon is compiled from the TS registry into parameterised SVG glyphs per semantic kind (stroke policy per size, late-bound ink), retired theme ids migrate, and the Explorer hides file glyphs while keeping their slot when Show file icons is off. FilePreviewIcon (previews.tsx / PreviewShell: the document shell with a text snippet, folder child count) is not ported; the audio card and other large icons draw the glyph at size.

groups.name: Product icons
groups.remaining: The seven product meanings (home, folder, local, cloud, cloud-upload, cloud-off, disclosure) are rendered from PRODUCT_ICONS into assets/ui-assets.json and requested as ProductIcon meanings with their optical stroke and CloudOff cutout. The disclosure's turn is drawn by each surface (the Explorer's follows its disclosure motion, not the 120ms CSS transition), and the mirrored collapsed disclosure of right-to-left layouts is not ported.

groups.name: Loading mark and placeholder material
groups.remaining: LoadingMark (rounded relay, xs/sm/md, inline and area layouts, five tones) and placeholder skeleton layers run on one App clock with the imported geometry; reduced motion holds the product's still figures. InlineLoading's mark-plus-label is composed per surface; the asset gallery has no recorded pixel comparison against Chromium.

groups.name: Ordered dither loading material
groups.reason: Retired in the native port: only the single rounded loading material is kept, and the Appearance page does not expose a loading-style picker.

groups.name: Floating notices
groups.remaining: FloatingNotice with its tone glyphs, message, inline and emphasised actions, busy state and dismiss control, and FloatingNoticeStack placement are native and used by clipboard notices, project place, folder status, the editor area, terminals and the workbench creation failure. Escape-to-dismiss while focus is inside the notice and FloatingNoticePortal's fallback stack are not ported; useDismissibleNotice's per-key dismissal is owned by each surface.

groups.name: Shared buttons and overflow dots
groups.remaining: po-button's neutral / primary / danger commands are drawn by the native Button variants on the surfaces that use it (Agents dialog, workbench close dialog), with a leading icon; there is no one-to-one tone API and no pixel comparison. The vertical OverflowDots is the overflow-dots.svg glyph on RowActionButton::more (three 2px squares, 2px apart); the horizontal variant of the editor pane actions trigger is not drawn because the native pane chrome lays its actions out inline.

groups.name: Scroll edge state
groups.remaining: useScrollEdgeState's 24px edge fade over a list that overflows by more than 1px is computed from GPUI scroll handles where a surface draws a fade (the Explorer's bottom fade into the footer, the Agent transcript's top fade). The is-scrollable classes useScrollableDescendantClasses puts on Changes lists have no native styling consumer.

groups.name: Sidebar primitives (rows, icon buttons, virtual lists)
groups.remaining: SidebarRow (tree, list and navigation variants, hover-revealed actions, selected backplates), the row icon buttons with their danger tint, section headers and groups are ui::components::sidebar. VirtualSidebarList / useVirtualSidebarWindow are GPUI uniform_list in the Explorer and Changes lists, which virtualise at any length rather than above SIDEBAR_VIRTUALIZATION_THRESHOLD. SidebarRoot, SidebarScrollArea and SidebarEmptyState are laid out by each surface (the Changes empty notes, Settings navigation) rather than as shared components.

groups.name: Workbench split tree and item model
groups.remaining: The shared split tree is re-expressed per owner: the right workbench's groups, tabs, splits, ratio bounds and minimum sizes (features::workbench::layout) and the editor's pane tree (editor::workbench::layout); closest-edge drops and split-fit checks are native. Moving or merging a whole group (move-group / merge-group, canMove/canMergeAuxiliaryWorkbenchGroup) is not ported, and stored layouts are checked by the Rust store instead of auxiliaryWorkbenchStateErrors.

groups.name: Shared-ui React and Electron plumbing
groups.reason: React/DOM/Electron plumbing with no native counterpart needed: a stable-identity React callback, a DOM probe that reads a CSS pixel custom property (native code reads the token from Theme), stripping Electron's "Error invoking remote method" IPC wrapper (Rust has no renderer IPC), and resolving public/ asset URLs against Vite's base (native assets are embedded by src/assets.rs).

groups.name: Unused shared-ui modules
groups.reason: Dead in the product: the file-open cache and request coordinator and the fileIconThemeRegistry compatibility re-export have no importers; EmptyState, IconButton, StatusBadge and SidebarList are exported from the shared-ui barrels but no product module renders them; ProjectsHeader (WorkspaceHeader) only renders when DataWorkspace's showHeader is true, and every product caller (DesktopDataWorkspaceSurface, FileModeApp, EditorPaneDocumentRuntime) passes showHeader={false}.

groups.name: Shared-ui fixtures, notes and performance probes
groups.reason: Contributor instructions, mock editor/tree fixtures with no importers, and the renderer performance tracker whose puppyone:renderer-performance events are consumed only by RendererPerformanceSmokeHarness; native timing uses Rust benches and frame budgets (tools/editor-frame-budgets.json).

groups.name: Window shell composition and workspace surfaces
groups.remaining: ProjectShell's composition (Header, project rail, Explorer column over the footer, editor area, right sidebar, the native window minimum from the pane minima plus the rail) and DesktopDataWorkspaceSurface's parts (Explorer with pins and Agent presence, the editor split view, file clipboard notices) are native in the Shell. The project rail is the compact rail only: the product's resizable, collapsible expanded rail is not ported. There is no surface registry: Data is the only workspace surface (the product already resolves git and cloud to it), Settings opens as its dialog, and a Cloud project reuses the same Explorer and editor instead of a second kept-alive location surface. The Plugins dialog and the AI edit response card (aiEditAssistEnabled) are not ported. Not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Workspace lifecycle and entry document
groups.remaining: Opening, creating, cloning, importing and switching projects, the launch's restore of the last one, the recent-project records and a nominated first document (a new project's Getting Started, a file window's file, initialOpenPath) are native in ProjectLifecycle. Not ported: the entry fallback for a folder entered without a nominated document or restored editors (resolveWorkspaceEntryDocument: Getting Started.md, then README, then index, then the first document by name), which opens nothing natively. Attaching and detaching extra folders (multiRootWorkspacesEnabled) is out of scope.

groups.name: Project entry launcher and flow
groups.remaining: The launcher (Create, Open a folder, Import) only routes, and the create, folder picker, template card and import dialogs follow one at a time on the window's dialog layer. ImportSourcePreview always shows GitHub and GitLab: the third mark the other-app-imports experiment adds (Obsidian) is not shown. The store link's read-failure dialog (templateLinkFailed with Retry) is not ported, since the link is handed over in process. Not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Homepage intro, first paint and analytics disclosure
groups.remaining: The empty Homepage's aperture intro (breathe 420ms, reveal 560ms, settle 120ms; the page inert until it ends), the one-time analytics disclosure after it (eligible, notice required, Basic; marked seen once shown) and the first-paint hold (the whole list in its final order, at most 4s, once per account, and the list hold after Home) are native. With reduced motion the intro is skipped rather than ending on the product's 220ms fallback; the dev-only notice preview (VITE_TELEMETRY_NOTICE_PREVIEW) is not ported. Not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Project configuration file
groups.remaining: <project>/.puppyone/config.json is read (normalized, unknown keys kept) when the repository settings load and written atomically on save, with the error kept beside the last good config. The 150ms reload after an outside edit (watchWorkspace) is not ported, and the config is held by the settings repository state rather than per window for every consumer.

groups.name: Loading layouts (page, inline, project opening)
groups.remaining: The LoadingMark itself (area and inline figures, sizes, tones) is shared. PageLoading, ProjectOpeningLoading (the mark held in the region the document will fill, its detail below) and InlineLoading are composed at each owner rather than as shared layout components, so the gap and label size follow each call site; not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Application render failure boundary
groups.reason: React error boundary that main.tsx wraps around the whole App to replace a render exception with a Refresh page. Native render functions return elements and cannot throw; failures are reported by their owners and process-level supervision is A-14/A-16 (as for the workbench render boundaries).

groups.name: Unused App Shell leftovers (unreachable)
groups.reason: Not reachable at v0.4.4 5e87974ef: projectBackupProviders.ts has no importer (only quality baselines list it); no element uses the .empty-workspace-starter-* classes of empty-workspace-onboarding.css (only styles.css imports it); DesktopShellAccessoryContext's provider is mounted by ProjectShell but its only consumer DesktopShellNavigationToolbarPortal is never rendered; DesktopSidebarRailNavigation and DesktopSidebarTopNavigation are only re-exported by navigation/index.ts and imported by a component test (the appearance resolves the sidebar navigation to bottom-horizontal only).

groups.name: Puppyone Git remote classification
groups.remaining: parsePuppyoneRemote, maskSecret / maskRemoteUrl and getPuppyoneRemote (one target; a remote whose fetch and push disagree, or two different targets, is a conflict) are repository_settings.rs; the canonical Project/Scope resolution that ignores access points (resolveCanonicalPuppyoneRemotes) is workspace::cloud::locator::canonical_locator, which counts identities over every remote URL but does not treat a canonical fetch paired with an access-point or foreign push as a conflict. describePuppyoneRemoteCandidates (the conflict diagnostic) and normalizeRemoteUrlForCompare are not ported.

groups.name: Version Control icon
groups.remaining: The product's glyph (same circles and paths, 2px round strokes) is assets/icons/version-control.svg, drawn by the Header's Changes tool, the Changes coachmark and the Appearance header-tools list. Its use in the device-folder Header and the unreachable setup entry state is not mirrored, and the stroke at 18px is not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Native web surface geometry, occlusion and pointer routing
groups.remaining: Native child views draw above the app in both stacks. Each wry WebView is placed from its element's paint every frame (place / place_clipped to the content mask, with corner radius when whole) and shows only while it painted in the last frame and no Shell dialog or popover is open (web_host::set_overlay / frame_drawn), which stands in for the occlusion leases, the layout leases and the shared settling frame clock; OS file drags over a WebView reach the pane because the view registers no drag types. Not ported: pointer passthrough and pointer-routing regions (resize lanes and in-app tab, pane and split drags crossing a WebView are not routed to the Shell), and trimming the outer pane chrome from the view's bounds (nativeSurfacePaneChrome) beyond clipping. useNativeSurfaceGeometry has no product caller in v0.4.4.

groups.name: Workbench data service and workspace content watch
groups.remaining: A window holds one admitted Workspace (local, Cloud or device folder) behind the provider facade: resources resolve against its root lease, documents hold their own watches and the Explorer session the root subscription, and a change invalidates documents and rereads loaded folders. The URI-routed multi-folder service (several Workspace Folders, cross-root copy, unavailable-folder stubs, per-composition watch ownership and retirement, folder-scoped change journal) belongs to multi-root composition and is not ported.

groups.name: Session transport: scoped operations
groups.remaining: signal, cancel and waitForScopedOperation (scope cancellation, ScopedOperationTimeoutError with its timeout) are native over the Agent's Canceller and the UI runtime's timer, used by AgentSessionController and AgentSessionReplica; own() and size, which no product caller uses, are not ported, and there is no dedicated Rust test.

groups.name: Session transport IPC plumbing (Electron)
groups.reason: Electron cross-process plumbing: receiving transferred MessagePorts from the preload, unwrapping results serialized across two IPC boundaries, and validating an out-of-process item-host termination receipt with a 5 s uncertainty timeout. The GPUI app runs the Agent host in-process (AgentHostHandle) and terminals as direct PTYs (platform::terminal), so there is no port, serialized envelope or item-host receipt; the item-host execution ownership gap is tracked in tools/agent-migration-map.json (agentExecutionClient).

groups.name: Data workspace shell and browser stylesheets
groups.remaining: Mixed feature stylesheets whose rules are re-expressed per element in Rust: the pin grid and files toggle, the list-end Create row, the Explorer column, the file-operation and workspace notice stacks, the footer bar and buttons and the external viewer chooser. Not ported: the rail and top navigation variants (see Sidebar footer navigation), viewer pack surface styles (Viewer Packs) and the remote update notice (unused in v0.4.4); file-list, inspector-column, risk-chip, mini-change-row, utility-workspace, changes-workspace and cloud-grid-host have no consumer in v0.4.4. Not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Git auto-commit settings (experimental)
groups.reason: Git auto-commit is out of scope; the hook only serves the auto-commit controls of RepositorySettingsViews (behind experimentalOptIn), which the Project, Git and Git Ignore settings group already lists as not ported.

groups.name: Unreachable source-control and data-workspace surfaces
groups.reason: Dead in v0.4.4. createSourceControlWorkspaceSurface and GitStatusView are only re-exported by source-control/index.ts and imported nowhere; VersionControlSetupState is used only by GitStatusView (the live setup action is GitRepositorySetupAction). RemoteUpdateNotice is imported by no module. changes.css is imported by styles.css but none of its selectors (change-dot, changes-content, diff-grid, diff-pane, review-row, review-list, section-kicker, browser-toolbar, ...) appear in any TS/TSX file.

groups.name: Automatic updates
groups.remaining: One update service checks 15 s after launch and every 6 h on the build's channel, downloads (unless automatic download is off), prepares the update beside the installed app and installs it on quit; the Header button, the Settings › General rows and the menu check follow its state. The renderer preview (?desktop-update-preview) is the capture-mode updates-fixture step. macOS only (no Windows or Linux installer path); acceptance against a real signed release feed is pending.

groups.name: Build identity
groups.remaining: The Settings › General version row (channel · version) and its copy button with the 1.5 s Copied state are native; the copied diagnostics name the app "PuppyOne GPUI" rather than "PuppyOne Desktop".

groups.name: Telemetry public disclosure link
groups.remaining: DISCLOSURE_URL is the same README#privacy address and opens from the Privacy row and the Homepage disclosure; no test pins the address.

groups.name: Feature flags and release gates
groups.remaining: account_available, cloud_enabled, host_devices_available/enabled and the HOST_DEVICES_AVAILABLE release gate (closed, as in v0.4.4) are features::flags and workspace::hosts::AVAILABLE. The account is available when the Cloud account service is installed rather than from a bundled flags.json; the payments decision reads experimental.payments at each entry (Plan, Agent compute routes, the managed-compute broker) without usePaymentsExperience's account gate; the cloudBilling flag, which nothing in the product reads, is not represented.

groups.name: Other computers: Computer access settings
groups.remaining: Settings › Computer access (behind the closed HOST_DEVICES_AVAILABLE gate) is native: this computer's sharing (pause, shared folders, start at login), the owner's other computers with presence, and the ⋯ menu whose Remove asks the system's warning first. Not compared against reference images.

groups.name: Markdown presentation overrides
groups.remaining: Only the default ('theme') presentation: headings and strong text take the active theme's --po-md-* values. The stored overrides (heading preset, strong weight and colour, the v1 migration) are neither imported from the appearance document's bySurface.markdown nor applied; v0.4.4 has no control that sets them (setMarkdownPresentation has no caller).

groups.name: Local workspace data port and main-process bridge
groups.remaining: The preload bridge itself has no native counterpart (one process, D-1): its calls are direct calls on the workspace provider, Git and window models, and createLocalDataPort's operations are the local workspace provider. connectWorkspaceCloudProject (Connect Existing Project) has no caller in the product and is not ported.

groups.name: Shell layout and global stylesheets
groups.remaining: Rules are re-expressed per element in Rust: the shell columns below the Header (shell.css), the pane group, right-sidebar stack and project menu rules (layout.css), the settings switch (base.css), the spinner (animations.css; Icon::spinning turns once per 900 ms) and the entry-state layout used by the Changes setup state and the Cloud publish task. The CSS reset, the location bar and classic scrollbar buttons (P3 Windows XP interface), the Cloud frame/rail and identity-button rules (no product consumer) and the unused pulse/ping/fade keyframes have no counterpart; reduced motion follows the system setting. Not pixel-compared.

groups.name: Viewer plugins (experimental)
groups.reason: Behind enableViewerPlugins (preferences.ts default false): App.tsx opens the Plugins dialog and the sidebar entry only when it is on. Plugins are out of scope for this round; plugins.css is imported globally but styles only these components.

groups.name: Cloud Connect Existing Project (unreachable)
groups.reason: createCloudGitConnectCoordinator serves cloud-git:connect-project, but its only renderer client, connectWorkspaceCloudProject (src/lib/localFiles.ts), has no caller in v0.4.4. The journal is otherwise read only by the first-publication coordinator to refuse publishing over a pending connect record, which nothing can create.

groups.name: Renderer DOM and build plumbing
groups.reason: No native counterpart needed: clipboard.ts wraps navigator.clipboard (native callers write with cx.write_to_clipboard); nativeTitleSuppression.ts strips DOM title tooltips; panelContract.ts is a React component type injected into the workbench; cascade.css only declares the CSS @layer order; viewer-surface-token-contract.json is read only by scripts/check-renderer-style-architecture.mjs (a build-time lint); utility-screens.css's only live rule is .application-render-fallback for the React ApplicationRenderBoundary, the rest (recording strip, utility table, panic undo, monitor footer) has no consumer.

groups.name: Test providers, smoke styles and mock data
groups.reason: Test and harness only: the localization testing providers and pseudo-locale catalog are imported only by tests; auxiliary-appearance-smoke.css serves the #auxiliary-appearance-smoke harness (AuxiliaryAppearanceSmokeHarness); mockData.ts is imported only by src/ai-edits/mockAiEdits.ts, which nothing imports.
